messages:
Priya Patel: Thanks for joining today's all-hands. Quick follow-up thread — collecting questions about engineering process items (release cadence, oncall rotation, quality bars, SLAs). We'll answer live in ~30m and then post a doc. Drop Qs here.

Alex Chen: Quick Q — are we still aiming for weekly release trains? past couple months looked more like two-week slips.

Priya Patel: Short answer: yes, weekly release train remains the target for hosted API. Dedicated/private customers may use biweekly frozen windows depending on compliance/manual cert steps. We'll document exceptions and the guardrails.

Samir Gupta: For the weekly train: what's the default canary window + rollback criteria? do we require perf-sig tests every train?

Priya Patel: Default canary window is 30m. Rollback criteria: error rate >0.5% above baseline OR p95 latency up >15% sustained for >5m. Perf sigs: smoke + core perf regression checks required pre-merge; full perf suite runs async and gates promoted rollouts for runtime-impacting PRs.

Marta López: Oncall Q: any update on moving rotations to 2-week? 1-week has been rough for some folks.

Alex Chen: Also — how many people are expected to be on pager for infra vs runtime teams?

Priya Patel: Oncall changes: we'll pilot 2-week rotations for infra starting next quarter; runtime oncall stays 1-week for now given current headcount. Typical coverage: runtime = 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra = 1 primary + 2 secondaries (we keep overlap for infra escalations). We'll share the rota template and shadowing plan.

Samir Gupta: Quality bars: are we enforcing a blanket codecov % across repos? PR requirements?

Priya Patel: No single blanket 80% across everything. Baseline expectation is tests + CI green. We recommend >=60% for most libs, and target >=80% for customer-facing services/runtime-critical components. Requirements: unit tests for new code, lint & typechecks must pass, and if you touch runtime paths add the "perf-test" PR label so the perf suite runs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-03-10 on hosted-api (build: 2026.03.10-7b2f).

Alex Chen: :eyes: Will the console show canary health per route (p50/p95/error-rate) or is it only a global view?

Priya Patel: Console will show route-level p50/p95 + error-rate and a "canary health" badge in Releases. We'll add more visible health markers for critical routes and upstream dependencies. Expect a doc with screenshots after the follow-up.

Marta López: SLAs — public hosted API SLA still 99.9? Any new SLO tiers for Dedicated customers?

Priya Patel: Hosted public SLA target remains 99.9 availability. Internally we operate to 99.95 SLOs for core infra. Dedicated customers can opt into 99.95 SLA with reserved capacity (contract + penalty). We'll publish an SLA matrix and examples next week.

Samir Gupta: Any concrete action items from this thread?

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll post an FAQ + one-pager with concrete examples and thresholds. @Marta López can draft the dedicated-vs-hosted release differences. @Alex Chen please sketch a console mock for the canary badge/route health. We'll collect feedback and update the public doc in #eng-docs.

Marta López: On it — I'll open a PR with the draft by EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen: I'll sketch the mock tonight and link the figma in the doc PR.

Priya Patel: Thanks all — we'll answer any live follow-ups at 2pm PT. Recording + doc will be dropped after the session. :hand:
